source_text: XIV. Οἱ δὲ οὐ καθήλωσαν μέν, προσέδησαν δὲ αὐτόν. Ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω τὰς χεῖρας ποιήσας καὶ προσδεθείς, ὥσπερ κριὸς ἐπίσημος ἐκ μεγάλου ποιμνίου εἰς προσφοράν, ὁλοκαύτωμα δεκτὸν τῷ θεῷ ἡτοιμασμένον, ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶπεν· Κύριε ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ὁ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ καὶ εὐλογητοῦ παιδός σου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πατήρ, δι᾽ οὗ τὴν περὶ σοῦ ἐπίγνωσιν εἰλήφαμεν, ὁ θεὸς ἀγγέλων καὶ δυνάμεων καὶ πάσης κτίσεως παντός τε τοῦ γένους τῶν δικαίων, οἳ ζῶσιν ἐνώπιόν σου· Εὐλογῶ σε, ὅτι κατηξίωσάς με τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ ὥρας ταύτης, τοῦ λαβεῖν μέρος ἐν ἀριθμῷ τῶν μαρτύρων ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ σου εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς αἰωνίου ψυχῆς τε καὶ σώματος ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ πνεύματος ἁγίου· ἐν οἷς προσδεχθείην ἐνώπιόν σου σήμερον ἐν θυσίᾳ πίονι καὶ προσδεκτῇ, καθὼς προητοίμασας καὶ προεφανέρωσας καὶ ἐπλήρωσας, ὁ ἀψευδὴς καὶ ἀληθινὸς θεός. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ περὶ πάντων σὲ αἰνῶ, σὲ εὐλογῶ, σὲ δοξάζω διὰ τοῦ αἰωνίου καὶ ἐπουρανίου ἀρχιερέως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀγαπητοῦ σου παιδός, δι᾽ οὗ σοὶ σὺν αὐτῷ καὶ πνεύματι ἁγίῳ δόξα καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς τοὺς μέλλοντας αἰῶνας, ἀμήν.
thought_title: Bound for the Fire and Praying Aloud
orientation: Polycarp stands bound on the ready pyre in the stadium and speaks his final prayer before the fire is lit.
pass_a_gloss: But they did not nail him, and they bound him. And he, having put his hands behind and having been bound, like a notable ram from a great flock for an offering, as a whole burnt offering acceptable to God that has been prepared, having looked up into heaven said: Lord God the almighty, the father of your beloved and blessed child Jesus Christ, through whom we received the knowledge about you, the God of angels and powers and of all creation and of the whole race of the righteous, who live before you; I bless you, because you counted me worthy of this day and this hour, to take a share in the number of the martyrs in the cup of your Christ for resurrection of eternal life both of soul and of body in imperishability of holy spirit; among whom may I be received before you today in a rich and acceptable sacrifice, just as you prepared beforehand and showed beforehand and fulfilled, O unlying and true God. Because of this also for all things I praise you, I bless you, I glorify you through the eternal and heavenly high priest Jesus Christ, your beloved child, through whom to you with him and with holy spirit be glory both now and into the coming ages, amen.

choices.why: brief glossary fixes this term as martyr for one who dies rather than deny Christ

choices.english: whole burnt offering acceptable to God
choices.why: keeps sacrificial language literal and unpolished rather than turning it into metaphor
paid means child or son here in address to the father, not servant in this prayer

choices.term: ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ σου
choices.english: in the cup of your Christ
choices.why: literal vessel image retained; not paraphrased as fate or suffering
ordinary cultic title kept literal without hyphenated compound

pass_b_english: They did not nail him but tied him fast. With his hands set behind his back and bound, like a choice ram taken from a great flock for an offering, a whole burnt offering acceptable to God and made ready, he looked up to heaven.

"Lord God Almighty, Father of your beloved and blessed child Jesus Christ, through whom we have received the knowledge of you, God of angels and powers and of all creation and of the whole race of the righteous who live in your presence, I bless you because you have counted me worthy of this day and hour to take a share in the number of the martyrs in the cup of your Christ, for the resurrection to eternal life of both soul and body in the imperishability of the Holy Spirit. May I be received among them before you today as a rich and acceptable sacrifice, just as you prepared beforehand and revealed beforehand and fulfilled it, O God who never lies and is true. For this reason I praise you for all things, I bless you, I glorify you, through the eternal and heavenly high priest Jesus Christ, your beloved child, through whom glory belongs to you with him and the Holy Spirit both now and for the ages to come. Amen."
